name: Chart-to-Speech Drill
description: Evaluates spoken conversion of visible chart information into patient-facing or team-facing clinical English.

anchors.90-100: Clear, controlled sentences with natural clinical phrasing
anchors.70-80: Minor errors but meaning is consistently clear
anchors.50-60: Understandable with repeated grammar or wording issues
anchors.30-40: Frequent errors make the message hard to follow
anchors.10-20: Language errors block most of the clinical message

anchors.90-100: All key chart facts, numbers, and abnormal results are accurate
anchors.70-80: Nearly all key facts are accurate; only minor omissions
anchors.50-60: Main idea is correct but some important facts or numbers are missing
anchors.30-40: Several inaccurate or unsafe chart details
anchors.10-20: Chart information is mostly wrong or misleading

anchors.90-100: Information is prioritized, concise, and organized for the audience
anchors.70-80: Mostly organized with a clear next step
anchors.50-60: Some structure but order or prioritization is uneven
anchors.30-40: Disorganized; listener must reconstruct the situation

anchors.90-100: Smooth delivery; numbers, units, times, and medication doses are easy to understand
anchors.70-80: Generally smooth; minor hesitation or number-reading issues
anchors.50-60: Noticeable hesitation; some numbers or units need repetition
anchors.30-40: Frequent stops or unclear numbers interfere with safety
anchors.10-20: Delivery blocks understanding of key chart details

anchors.90-100: Perfectly adapts register: concise team language or plain patient language as needed
anchors.50-60: Generally polite but sometimes too technical, vague, or casual
anchors.10-20: Unprofessional or confusing for the audience

checklist.item: identified the patient and situation clearly
used the right register for the audience (team vs patient)
organized information in a safe clinical sequence
gave a clear next step, recommendation, or confirmation
checked understanding or confirmed read-back when appropriate
